text:
### Observed differences

- The elapsed time from the completion of A02 to the completion of A08 roughly halved. In the earlier window the gap was typically about 0.88 hours (median; mean about 0.86 h, middle half roughly 0.79–0.94 h), while in the later window it was typically about 0.44 hours (mean about 0.45 h, middle half roughly 0.41–0.49 h) — about 25 minutes less per occurrence. [TWAIT001]
- The gap also became more consistent: its standard deviation fell from about 0.11 to about 0.06 hours, while the number of observed gaps stayed similar (29 before vs 30 after), so this is a shift in the typical gap rather than a change in how often the pair occurs. [TWAIT001]
- This timing difference is unusually large for a random re-split — it is bigger than in about 1999 of 2000 reference comparisons — but it is the only item that qualified among the 69 units tested. [TWAIT001]
- No control-flow difference reached the thresholds: 0 of 52 tested units qualified, in line with the roughly 0.26 items expected by chance in an unchanged process. [screening]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The only qualifying signal is a single time item (the A02-to-A08 completion gap halving) from a family where about 0.008 items were expected by chance, and with only about 30 observations per window such a lone extreme cannot be separated from sampling variation [TWAIT001, screening].
